chemistryNotes: Curriculum context remains Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1, using the retained local IGCSE sources and existing reviewed qualifications; no OCR A Level coverage claim.
SOLVENT and SOLUTE teacher wording is restricted explicitly to a solid dissolved in a liquid. Solutes are not universally solids and solvents are not universally liquids.
Electron relative mass zero is accepted only as a whole-number approximation, alongside the requested fractions; it is not a claim that electrons have zero mass.
Preserve dilute acid, aqueous reagents, anhydrous copper sulfate, reaction conditions and the location of observations while shortening field answers.
Bromide precipitate is cream. Off-white was retained verbatim in the teacher export but omitted from the working answer to avoid accepting the chloride observation.

Contains matching is retained where requested as an authoring mode. Runtime implementation must still reject contradictory/negated responses and preserve formula case, charge, order and distinct parts.
The earlier export displayed whole-field matching modes on MCQ/numeric records. These irrelevant modes are normalised to null; numeric values/ranges and MCQ options are separate contracts.
